why: An outpost Defend's loss budget is priced as it commits and only a re-form re-prices it, so its losses past the budget end it: our bot in three mutually hostile seats, where alpha camps the exit beta's E18S6 Defend enters by. On the old rule every death re-priced the budget to losses so far plus the predicted dead, so the bound was never crossed: beta's Defend opened t4631 (priced a win losing 1) counted 52 lost (about 15 bodies dead, the rest spent bodies healed and drafted again) by t5355, its casts walking in one at a time. Each Defend in every seat, at whichever tick it opens, loses at most the bodies of the tick it quits on past its budget (defend 3 there: 47 past it on 8c0c5ded, before the fix; at most 0 on seeds 1-5 after, every seat opening Defends on every seed). Bodies lost over the run, each seat, are a guardrail 1.5x the seed 1-5 maxima as the bot's own close rows count them, a close's last tick's dead with them (alpha 0, beta 1, gamma 1: 0, 1, 1; the count before took a close's dead only from its last Memory or its bodies' tombstones in the rooms it targeted: alpha 0, beta 1, gamma 4). Self-play, since only our own Defend's accounting is read
